allies.rationale_text: Experimentation gives variation-and-selection the real-world testing discipline needed to separate promising variants from weak ones.
allies.source_quote: Treating solutions as a portfolio of experiments allows real-world data to steer the subsequent direction.
allies.affinity_rationale: Variation-and-selection IS experimentation; generating multiple approaches maximizes discovery probability
allies.activation_condition: When generating and testing multiple approaches maximizes the probability of finding optimal solutions

allies.rationale_text: Base-rates keep variation-and-selection from choosing attractive variants that collapse once the selection step is checked against reference-class reality.
allies.source_quote: The Outside View provides the objective standard necessary for the Selection phase.
allies.affinity_rationale: Canonical describes the outside view as providing the objective standard necessary for the selection phase
allies.activation_condition: When reference-class data provides the objective standard for evaluating which variations to select

antagonists.rationale_text: Curse-of-knowledge undermines variation-and-selection by causing experts to leap directly to an overarching principle, skipping the divergent generation of concrete building blocks the model requires.
antagonists.source_quote: The Curse of Knowledge: Experts suffer from the inability to recall what it was like not to know something. Their expertise often causes them to immediately jump to the 'answer' or overarching principle (a form of premature Selection). This inhibits the necessary Variation needed to simplify ideas into the concrete, elementary building blocks required for effective communication or teaching.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Canonical states expertise causes premature selection by jumping to answers, inhibiting necessary variation
antagonists.activation_condition: When expertise causes premature selection by jumping to familiar answers, inhibiting necessary variation

structured_tensions.tension_text: Variation-and-selection conflicts with status-quo-bias when exploration of new options is blocked by attachment to the current solution.
structured_tensions.source_quote: variation-and-selection vs status-quo-bias: variation-and-selection conflicts with status-quo-bias (status quo bias) when variation and Selection challenges the Status Quo Bias by encouraging exploration of new options rather than sticking to existing solutions.

structured_tensions.tension_text: Variation-and-selection conflicts with commitment-bias when early commitments stop the team from generating or fairly selecting better alternatives.
structured_tensions.source_quote: variation-and-selection vs commitment-bias: variation-and-selection conflicts with commitment-bias (commitment and consistency bias) when commitment and Consistency Bias can hinder the Variation phase by discouraging deviation from initial choices, opposing the model's emphasis on exploring diverse options.

structured_tensions.tension_text: Variation-and-selection conflicts with confirmation-bias when the search space is narrowed to options that merely confirm the current belief.
structured_tensions.source_quote: variation-and-selection vs confirmation-bias: variation-and-selection conflicts with confirmation-bias (confirmation bias) when variation search is constrained to options that confirm existing beliefs, preventing the model from discovering superior alternatives.
